comparison: Both evaluate patient-specific model predictions (C35, C36, C88, C89). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to small sample size and mixed validation (8/10 matches), while peer reviewers are also UNCERTAIN, citing lack of empirical validation with patient cells and overlooked discrepancies. Strong agreement on uncertainty.

Both address JNK inhibitor combination experiments (C23, C24, C25). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, viewing experimental validation as confirming computational predictions. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, arguing that combination shows no benefit beyond JNKi alone and lacks proper synergy analysis. Major disagreement on interpretation of same data.

Both evaluate the computational prediction of JNK combination therapy (C22, C83). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as key discovery. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, identifying circular reasoning: training data contained the very combination being 'predicted', creating a self-fulfilling prophecy. Fundamental methodological disagreement.

Both address JNK's mechanistic role in cell cycle regulation (C27-C31, C84). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, finding mechanism plausible and data-consistent. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, not challenging these molecular findings. Agreement on mechanistic claims.

Both evaluate PCA analysis and experimental clustering (C13-C15, C75-C76). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, viewing results as internally consistent. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to presentation issues: unclear cytokine stimulation status, confusing figures, and challenging interpretation. Disagreement stems from clarity concerns.

Both address Boolean model structure and signaling rewiring (C18, C19, C80). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, finding network architecture well-documented. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting altered signaling networks as demonstrated. Agreement on structural findings.

Both evaluate model validation against known TKI sensitivity (C21, C81). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, viewing validation as critical for model credibility. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting models' ability to reproduce differential sensitivity. Agreement on basic validation.

Both assess overall study conclusions and clinical potential (C93-C95). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, viewing proof-of-concept as reasonable despite limitations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with mixed views: potential step forward but fundamental concerns about methodology and validation undermine clinical validity claims. Moderate disagreement on overall assessment.

Both address network construction methodology (C10, C46, C73). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, finding PKN construction well-documented. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, praising data availability and code sharing. Agreement on methodological rigor.

Both evaluate experimental reproducibility and measurement quality (C12, C49). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting quantified reproducibility. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED through implicit acceptance (no challenges raised). Agreement on technical quality.
